title: Predictive Autoscale + Reserved Mix SKU pilot for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Aisha Rao
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers want predictable baseline throughput for critical workloads but also need burst capacity for seasonal spikes. Current product offers reserved GPUs (committed) and separate burst policies that are either manual or fixed-cost credits. This ticket proposes a new pilot SKU that bundles a lower-cost reserved baseline with a predictive autoscale burst pool priced by effective GPU-hour credits and governed by a model-driven eligibility window.

Goal: Validate whether a bundled Reserve+PredictiveAutoscale product increases committed ARR, reduces churn for irregular-heavy customers, and preserves margin vs. offering pure reservation or pure on-demand burst.

Scope: 1) Define pricing formula for baseline reservation (per-GPU-month) + predictive burst credits (per-GPU-hour) with a sliding discount curve tied to commit size. 2) Define SLA tiers (Bronze/Silver/Gold) mapped to baseline commit and burst SLAs (latency targets, preemption policies, regional fallback). 3) Design pilot enrollment flow and telemetry to measure utilization, revenue uplift, unit economics, latency impact, and customer satisfaction. 4) Create legal/SQ questionnaire addendum draft for pilot customers describing billing, data isolation, and incident SLAs.
acceptance_criteria: Pricing formula documented with worked examples for 3 commit sizes (small/medium/large)
SLA tier matrix that maps commit bands to availability and burst priority defined
Pilot contract addendum and security questionnaire responses drafted and reviewed by Legal and Security
Telemetry dashboard prototype showing baseline utilization, burst consumption (GPU-hours), latency percentiles, and incremental revenue
Sign up of at least 6 pilot customers across startups and mid-market with different usage patterns
Rollout decision checklist and go/no-go recommendations produced by experiment end
comments: 2025-11-03 Aisha Rao: Kickoff — outlined customer problem and initial pricing levers. Spoke with Sales (Lena Ortiz) — they have 12 prospects with intermittent monthly spikes who asked for a simpler bundled offer.

2025-11-05 Marco Chen: Engineering feasibility sync — runtime team flagged two implementation gaps: a) need a predictive signal to pre-provision KV cache to avoid cold-start latency; b) billing system must track GPU-hour credits with per-request attribution. Estimated 3 sprints for infra changes if prioritized.
2025-11-07 Design review (Samir Patel): UX for pilot enrollment modal and usage dashboard mocked. Recommend showing projected monthly spend under 3 forecast scenarios (steady, spike, seasonal).

2025-11-10 Legal note (K. Huang): Draft addendum must include termination rights for non-forecasted abuse, and explicit mapping of burst price to GPU-hour unit. We'll loop Security for KMS/HSM language.

2025-11-12 Finance (R. Gupta): Modeled ARR uplift vs. cannibalization. Baseline assumption: 15% of on-demand spend converts to committed at 25% lower baseline rate, bursts priced at ~1.6x baseline GPU-hour. Need sensitivity analysis on utilization delta.

2025-11-14 Engineering PRD update: Added requirement for predictive eligibility window (12-48 hours) leveraging recent telemetry signals. If prediction confidence < threshold, fallback to normal burst rules.
2025-11-16 Sales feedback: Proposed pilot pitch and email template. Sales requests a 90-day pilot with milestone checkpoints and usage caps to reduce procurement friction.

2025-11-18 Security review (M. Alvarez): Security questionnaire draft reviewed. Action: add SOC2/HIPAA status and default encryption-at-rest language. Security requested a short SLA incident runbook example.

2025-11-20 Marco Chen: Updated plan after infra scoping — reduced initial infra changes by implementing predictive signals in the control plane + soft throttling; left KV pre-warm as phase 2. Adjusted estimate to 8 points.
